text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and well grounded. Every number matches the card: 30.8% of 2,372 claims, 4.3% expected, risk-adjusted score 21.24, z 4.01, 32% low-complexity, 58 records, 8 of 18 (44%) vs 12%, and 4 of 48. The cited claims fit their sentences. C0076627, C0077120 and C0077316 are in the below-billed examples. C0077120 is also in the low-complexity list as a 32-year-old with hyperlipidemia. C0076565, C0076824 and C0076832 are low-complexity 99215 claims with the right ages and conditions. The language is cautious ('reason to review, not a finding'), and the next steps are concrete. The weaknesses are small. The summary does not flag what is missing, such as the small documented sample (2.4% of claims) or how the records were selected. It cites no high-complexity 99215 claims or supported examples for balance. Three of the six examples are low-complexity claims with no documentation, and C0076832 (atrial fibrillation with J06.9) is a weak illustration. It also does not mention that 99215 share rises with complexity for this provider, though it is still high at every level.","problems":["Does not flag the small documented sample (58 of 2,372 claims, 2.4%) or that records may not be representative.","No balancing evidence, such as the 4 documented 99215 claims that were supported at high MDM, or the high-complexity 99215 claims.","Three of the six cited examples have no documentation, so they support only the complexity point, not the documentation point; the 'with 1 chronic condition' framing for atrial fibrillation is a weak example.","The 4-of-48 data-reviewed finding is stated without explaining why it matters or what to check."]}
